It matters here because a direct `#[cfg(test)]` unit test of `render_scene` in `apps/browser/src/capture.rs` is built under the browser's default features, which name no accessibility (decision/browser-accessibility-off-by-default). The test must not rely on, or turn on, an accessibility-gated item.

Trap for this chunk: any dev-dependency or crate edge added to the browser crate for the test could pull `accessibility` in transitively and change the browser's feature graph. The scope rules out new carriers and every other crate, so the browser's manifest should stay untouched.

That bears on what `render_scene` returns, because the function reads `doc.viewport().scale_f64()`. A test that asserts the returned `(u32, u32)` for a set viewport has to choose its inputs with that physical-versus-scale relationship in mind. No later amendment has changed either row.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — (the shot's answer line, no font refused) added a Typography Loading rule: if a driver `screenshot`'s font context resolves no `sans-serif` family, the shot is refused `fonts-unavailable` and nothing is painted, so text is never silently skipped. It also set the shot's `{"width","height","png"}` answer line on the cli surface. This is the precedent closest to a direct test that paints a scene headless and reads its size. It is a trap if the test's document holds text and no font is registered. Note that this rule belongs to the driver's screenshot path, not to the browser's `capture.rs`; the browser's `RenderSize::resolve` path is outside it.

body: The scene render's returned size: the width and height in pixels it returns for a document's viewport, asserted directly by a new unit test for two inputs of different sizes, each larger than 1 px in both dimensions, so that all four constant replacements fail it.

Indirect: the expected size the test asserts is the viewport size derived from the document's viewport and its scale; the logical viewport and its scale rule decide what value is correct, and the test must assert that value, not a hard-coded guess that ignores the scale.

The new test lives inside the browser crate's own test module and builds what the render takes, a document with a set viewport and a paint scene, under the crate's default features; it reaches the render function directly, not through the screenshot path, since both callers discard the size.

Invariant: what the browser paints and saves stays as it is; the scene render's painting and both callers (the screenshot capture, which resolves its own size before rendering, and the anyrender scene capture) behave as before, held by the existing browser tests; if the fork removes the return value, only the unused size goes.

body: The returned size of render_scene: a new unit test asserts it for one input whose viewport is wider and taller than 1 px and for a second input of a different size, so each of the four constant mutants (both dimensions at most 1) fails it and the value is shown to follow the input.
The new test lives in the capture file's own inline test module and reaches render_scene there, without widening the function's visibility or adding a seam for the test.

The test builds what render_scene takes inside the browser crate under its default features: a document with a set viewport and scale, and a scene painter written by hand in the test, with no mocking library and its data stated in code.
The expected sizes are pinned as literal values in the test, not recomputed by the code under test or by the same size resolution the capture path uses.
The test is controlled red-before-green: it is shown to fail when the returned size is replaced by each of the four constants, and to pass on the real code.

The mutation tier: a cargo-mutants run under nextest of the browser package, even of these four alone, is started only on the founder's word, as an operator entry or a fork put to him, on the dev host only and never in CI; the plan carries no gate that runs it by itself.
The mutation baseline is read per unit: the audit's survivors list for the browser holds these four, and the chunk's outcome is each one read caught by the test or kept by the founder's word.

The fork between a test that pins an unused return value, removing that value from upstream browser code (adding to the upstream divergence of an app the fork does not develop), and keeping the four on the founder's word is the founder's to rule.
No change to what the browser paints or saves, and no new carrier, verb, log field, span, env read or listener: the capture path's behaviour stays as it is whichever way the fork goes.
The browser crate's own test run is the check that holds the new test green; a per-package green is not read as the workspace green.

body_fields.convention: a new unit test sits in an inline test module in its source file
a new unit test pins its expected value as a literal, is controlled red-before-green, and its failure prints no argument value
a new test uses hand-written stand-ins, never a mocking library
a new test's data is stated in code, nothing seeded
a regression test documents and is named for what it guards
